name: When should I repair or replace my water heater if it's not heating?

mainEntity.name: When should I repair or replace my water heater if it's not heating?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deciding whether to repair or replace depends on several factors. Consider the age of your unit; water heaters typically last 8-12 years. If yours is older and repairs are costly, replacement might be more economical in the long run. Frequent repairs, signs of leakage, or insufficient hot water after a fix also point towards replacement. If the issue is minor and the unit is relatively new, a repair is usually the better option. A professional plumber can help you weigh the options.
acceptedAnswer.description: If your water heater is old (8-12 years), has frequent issues, or leaks, replacement might be better. For newer units with minor problems, repair is often sufficient.
